title: Learned causal box refiner + retrain of the GRU/Mamba keypoint position memory on our pose detector outputs
written: 2026-11-15 17:00 KST, before any detector run, any validation number or any training
user_decision: 2026-11-15 '2번부터 하자': learned causal box refiner first, trained together with the retraining of the GRU/Mamba keypoint position memory (same data)

near.note: device default near pose model (YOLO26m-pose body box)

data.inference: fp32 PyTorch on the GPU server, batch 4, input = the 640x480 grey picture as 3 equal channels (0..255, /255 inside), the ONE-TO-MANY head (cv2/cv3/cv4/cv4_kpts), i.e. the same branch the device DXNN files export (build_bodybox_kpt.py SixHeads). Decode = post.cpp decode_raw (anchor centre +- ltrb distances x stride), score = sigmoid(person logit). NMS = post.cpp nms_decoded: per class, candidates score > 0.001, stable sort by score, greedy, suppress IoU > 0.7, at most 300 kept. Keypoints of a kept box = the raw keypoint head at the same anchor, decoded as detect_frame.attach_kpts (x = (raw_x + col + 0.5) * stride, same for y, visible = sigmoid).
data.kept_detections: person boxes with score > 0.10 (ByteTrack low threshold: lower boxes are never used by the tracker; KeepID also uses >= 0.1) and height <= 1440 px (detect_frame.drop_giant). Kept exactly: greedy NMS in score order means the kept set above 0.10 does not depend on candidates below 0.10. Device-only filters not reproducible on 8-bit public data (warmth veto on 16-bit raw) are not applied.
data.picture_size: device size 640x480. TMOT train: the 640x480 copy (rows 16..496 of the 640x512 FLIR frames, same cut as the device canvas). TMOT val: the 640x480 copy tmot_val_20261114 (same cut). DanceTrack: the existing grey 640x480 copy = letterbox: 1920x1080 scaled to 640x360 and padded with grey 114 above and below (content rows 60..420), the same picture the FastTrackTr thermal training used.
data.coordinates: everything in the server's frame canvas: x as the picture, y = picture y + 16 (640x512 canvas, picture rows 16..496), edges of the position memory features 0 / 640 and 16 / 496 exactly as position_memory.py.
data.camera_motion: GMC per frame = the server's camera_motion.GMC (Ultralytics sparseOptFlow, downscale 2) with the device options --gmc-corners 300 --gmc-mindist 5, on the 640x512 canvas made like detect_frame.to_canvas (edge rows replicated). Warp previous -> current frame, identity on the first frame.
data.frame_rates: TMOT about 9.3 fps (seq18-21, val seq17 and seq22 about 5 fps), from the thermal file time stamps; DanceTrack 20 fps. The device camera runs about 25-30 fps: a known mismatch, reported.

association.rule: Ground truth (gt) = full person box of the dataset; ours = body box (head top to hip, may reach outside the picture). Per frame, Hungarian assignment of kept detections to gt boxes with cost 1 - IoU(detection, expected body box of the gt box). Gates: detection clipped to the picture lies at least 50 % inside the gt box (containment) and |detection top - expected top| <= 0.25 x gt height (top alignment). Pass 1: expected body box from one global relation per dataset (median over train-split pairs that pass the gates with IoU of the plain top-aligned prior >= 0.3). Pass 2: expected body box from the track's own median relation (tracks with >= 5 pass-1 matches, else the global one); accept IoU >= 0.4.
association.report: match rate = share of gt boxes (gt height >= 24 px) with an associated detection, per dataset and detector; share of detections with score >= 0.25 associated to some gt box.

target.rule: Per gt track: relation = median over its associated frames of (dx = (cx_det - cx_gt) / h_gt, dtop = (top_det - top_gt) / h_gt, log width ratio, log height ratio = log(h_det / h_gt)). Target body box in every frame of the gt track = gt box mapped through that median relation. Tracks with fewer than 5 associated frames get no target. The width ratio is taken against the gt width or the gt height, whichever gives the smaller median absolute deviation of the associated detections on the TRAIN split (chosen once, before validation).
target.report: fit where both exist: median IoU(target, associated detection), share IoU >= 0.5, median centre error / target height, per dataset and detector.

splits.rule: by sequence. TMOT train (24, numeric order): index % 5 == 2 -> val-A, rest -> train. TMOT val (6) -> val-B. DanceTrack train (36, name order): index % 9 == 4 -> val-B, index % 9 == 8 -> val-A, rest -> train. DanceTrack val (4) -> val-B.
splits.use: train = fitting; val-A = every choice (epochs, learning rate, initialisation, One Euro parameters); val-B = report only, never used for a choice. The TMOT val sequences are also used by a separate final-benchmark job for detector scoring; here they are only val-B.

position_memory.models: gru_kpt (GRUCell 68 -> 64, head 4) and mamba_kpt (MambaArm d 48) exactly as m5_kpt_motion_v2.Net, so the server's PosKpt numpy forward reads the files unchanged
position_memory.inputs: exactly the server feature builder (position_memory._kp_feat_seen / pos_predict_kpt) on our detector boxes and keypoints, both detectors pooled: per gt track the tracker-like Kalman filter (Ultralytics XYWH, GMC warp after predict, lost tracks predicted with vw = vh = 0, re-initiated after more than 30 lost frames), innovation against the warped prediction, seen-frame feature also for the run start (velocity 0 / innovation 0 for a new track), history = the current run of consecutive seen frames (at most 20, at least 4 = KP_MINOBS); lost path = the server's plain path (warp of the anchor+2 frame used for steps 1 and 2 as pos_predict_kpt does), keypoint visible = sigmoid >= 0.5, 15 lost steps.
position_memory.anchors: every seen frame t with >= 4 features; targets = target body boxes of t+1..t+15 where they exist. 'sim' = detector still has the person at t+1 (we hide it), 'real' = no associated detection at t+1 (real detector miss), 'syn' = m5 v2 vanish augmentation (occluder sweep, fixed seed 12345) on the validation sequences.
position_memory.training: AdamW wd 1e-4, cosine to 2 %, batch 512, up to 30 epochs, loss = m5 loss (smooth L1 of centre / true height and log size + 1 - GIoU). Augmentation as m5 v2 --aug 1 (time reversal, left-right flip with COCO flip order, half frame rate, synthetic vanish) with the warps transformed consistently; no synthetic jitter (inputs are real detector outputs). Each epoch: all TMOT train anchors + DanceTrack train anchors of every 3rd frame (random offset per epoch).
position_memory.configs: two per arm: (a) from scratch lr 2e-3, (b) initialised from the current posetrack18 file lr 5e-4. Choice of config and epoch on val-A by sel = (score_all + score_syn) / 2 (m5 v2 rule), TMOT and DanceTrack val-A anchors pooled.
position_memory.metric: m5: per horizon h in (5, 10, 15) mean of min(centre error / target height, 2); score = mean over the three horizons. Groups all / sim / real / syn. TMOT and DanceTrack separately, per detector and pooled over detectors.
position_memory.compared: plain Kalman path (zero correction), the CURRENT files pos_gru_kpt_posetrack18_20261114 / pos_mamba_kpt_posetrack18_20261114 (keypoint inputs 1 and 2 zeroed as the server does for 'posetrack' names), the new files; all fed the same detector inputs.
position_memory.beats_rule: a new file beats the current one when the val-B 'all' score is lower with the per-sequence bootstrap 90 % interval of (new - current) below 0, in both TMOT and DanceTrack (pooled over the two detectors). Otherwise reported as not shown.

box_refiner.model: GRUCell(70 -> 48) + linear head 4 (zero init = raw detector box). Input per seen frame: the 68 position-memory seen-frame numbers computed with the refiner's own tracker-like Kalman filter with GMC warp (box change against the warped previous box) + 2 camera numbers (GMC shift of the previous box centre / box height). History up to and including the current frame only; state reset at a new run (track id not drawn in the previous frame, or a jump of more than 1.5 box heights).
box_refiner.output: corrected current box: centre = detector centre + 0.5 x height x tanh(o[:2]), size = detector size x exp(ln 1.5 x tanh(o[2:]))
box_refiner.loss: per frame smooth L1 (beta 0.02) of the error vector e = ((cx - cx_t) / h_t, (cy - cy_t) / h_t, log(w / w_t), log(h / h_t)) + 1.0 x smooth L1 of its second difference over time (jitter relative to the target)
box_refiner.training: per gt-track runs of the train split (both detectors), pieces of at most 256 frames, truncated BPTT with chunks of 64 frames (state carried inside a piece), AdamW wd 1e-4, cosine to 2 %, batch 64 pieces, up to 30 epochs
box_refiner.configs: lr in {2e-3, 5e-4}; config and epoch chosen on val-A by the validation loss (same formula as the loss) on the server-like rows (below)
box_refiner.evaluation_rows: server-like: the server's ByteTrackTracker (Python, mode bytetrack, n_init 3 = --confirm-ms 130 at these frame rates, class gate, edge birth 0.5, GKF + GMC warp, position memory Kalman) on the kept detections; every output row whose detection is associated to a gt track with a target. Methods run per tracker id over its rows (state reset as on the server).
box_refiner.baselines: raw detector box; the tracker's output box (Kalman posterior); One Euro filter (Casiez et al., CHI 2012) on the detector box per tracker id: centre (cx, cy) with one (min_cutoff, beta), log w / log h with another, d_cutoff 1 Hz, speed term in box heights per second, dt = 1 / sequence fps, previous state moved by the GMC warp before each step (camera compensation); parameters chosen on val-A by a grid (min_cutoff in 0.05..8 Hz, beta in 0..3) minimising the same validation loss; learned refiner.
box_refiner.camera_test: One Euro with vs without the warp compensation on DanceTrack (moving camera) and on TMOT with a synthetic pan added in coordinates (boxes, targets and warps shifted by the same smooth pan, 0..6 px per frame); same for the refiner's Kalman features
box_refiner.metrics: accuracy: centre error / target height (capped 2), |log w ratio|, |log h ratio|, IoU with the target; jitter: RMS of the second difference of centre / target height and of log h, output vs target on the same frames (three consecutive rows of one id); lag: centre error and signed along-motion error by target speed bin (0-0.01, 0.01-0.03, 0.03-0.1, > 0.1 heights per frame); gimbal aim point (top + 0.37 x height): error / target height and its jitter; device cost: numpy ms per track per frame (PC and an estimate for the device CPU).
box_refiner.report: val-B per dataset (TMOT, DanceTrack), per detector and pooled; per-sequence bootstrap (2000 draws, seed 0) 90 % intervals for each method and for differences refiner - raw / tracker / One Euro.

server_integration: src/track/box_refine.py, default off, applied only to the rows drawn and sent to the gimbal (never the tracker state or association); modes off | euro | gru via /rules/set?box_refine=...

amendment_1.written: 2026-11-15 17:25 KST, after the coordinator's two messages, before any detection result was looked at (the first detector run was stopped and restarted for a GPU memory fix) and before any validation number
amendment_1.why: (1) Verified public evaluation (final_eval_20261115): the far detector F gives whole-person boxes for people under about 100 px gt height (box / gt 1.0-1.16) and head-to-hip boxes above (about 0.54 of gt); E is about 0.65 of gt at 50-100 px. A per-track median relation would mix box definitions. (2) User: '변할 때 자연스럽게 변해야 한다, 확확 변하면 안 된다' - the box and the aim point must change smoothly in every situation (detector switch, the 100 px shape change, occlusion, picture edge).
amendment_1.association_change: cost = 1 - max(IoU(detection, expected head-to-hip box of the gt box), IoU(detection, gt box)) so that both box definitions are associated; gates unchanged (containment >= 0.5 of the clipped detection inside the gt box, top within 0.25 gt heights); accept max IoU >= 0.35. Pass 0 uses the prior (top aligned, height 0.55, width 0.9 of the gt box, same x centre) to measure the global relation, pass 1 uses the measured global relation. The per-track pass of the first version is dropped.
amendment_1.refiner_target: ONE fixed head-to-hip relation per dataset (gt conventions differ between TMOT and DanceTrack): medians of (dx / h_gt, dtop / h_gt, log(w_det / w_gt or / h_gt, chosen as before), log(h_det / h_gt)) over train-split associated pairs of both detectors with gt height >= 100 px and detector box height / gt height in 0.40..0.75 (the head-to-hip regime). Target = gt box mapped through it in every frame. The per-track median relation is kept only as a secondary comparison.
amendment_1.position_memory_target: primary = the detector's own box at that person size: per detector and dataset, median relation in gt-height bins (< 35, 35-50, 50-70, 70-100, 100-140, 140-200, >= 200 px) from train associated pairs, linearly interpolated in log gt height between bin centres. Reason: the position memory's box is written into the lost track's Kalman state and must overlap the SAME detector's next box to re-associate; moving it to a head-to-hip box would break re-association for far-detector small people. Secondary = the global head-to-hip target. Training of the new files uses the primary target.
amendment_1.refiner_size_bound: size correction bound widened to x/ 2.5 (ln 2.5) so a whole-person box (about 1.85 x the head-to-hip height) can be mapped to the head-to-hip box; centre bound stays 0.5 box heights.

smoothness.detector_switch_training: refiner training sequences splice the near and far detector outputs of the same gt person at random switch frames (each piece: with probability 0.5 one or more switches, gaps between switches 1-8 s), refiner state kept across the switch
smoothness.occlusion_augmentation: with probability 0.3 per piece an occluder enters from the bottom or one side over 3-10 frames, stays 0-40 frames, leaves over 3-10 frames: keypoints under it hidden; with probability 0.5 the detector box also shrinks to the visible part (+ noise); target unchanged
smoothness.switch_evaluation: val-A / val-B detection streams spliced at the sequence level (all people at once, as the device switches): switch every 2-6 s (uniform, seed 1), starting detector alternating; the tracker is run on the spliced stream; methods run per tracker id with state kept across switches
smoothness.metrics_added: per method (raw / tracker / One Euro / refiner, + target as reference): p95 and p99 over frames of |delta height| / target height and |delta aim point| / target height between consecutive rows of one id; largest single-frame jump per track (median and p90 over tracks); the same at detector-switch frames (switch frame and the next 0.5 s) and at size-crossing frames (gt height crossing 100 px, +- 2 frames), at occlusion events (associated detection loses >= 4 visible keypoints within 3 frames) and edge events (target box crossing the picture edge); box-definition consistency by gt size bin (< 50, 50-100, >= 100 px): median and IQR of output height / target height. All refiner and position-memory metrics also by gt size bin.
smoothness.server_blend: independent of the learned model: on a detector change each track keeps its filter state, and the drawn / gimbal box goes from the old to the new box over a window T: the box offset (centre / height, log size) between the track's last output and its first new-detector output decays linearly to 0 over T. T chosen on val-A switch streams from {0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8} s by the validation loss, separately for raw, One Euro and refiner. Default off on the server.
smoothness.selection_loss: unchanged formula (accuracy + 1.0 x second-difference jitter term); on val-A it is computed on the switch streams and the no-switch streams together

amendment_1.valB_note: TMOT val is used here as val-B (report only); it is therefore no longer a one-time final test for the whole system
